evals.prompt: Create a Discord moderation bot with TypeScript. I need ban, kick, warn, timeout, and purge commands. It should log all mod actions to a designated channel. I'll host it on a VPS with Docker. I already have a bot token and a test server.
evals.expected_output: A complete TypeScript project scaffold with discord.js v14, slash commands for ban/kick/warn/timeout/purge, Prisma schema with ModAction and GuildConfig models, a moderation log event system, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml with PostgreSQL, and proper error handling.

assertions.text: Output includes a package.json with discord.js, @prisma/client, typescript, and pino as dependencies
Output includes a tsconfig.json with strict mode enabled and ES2022 target
Output includes a .env.example with DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, DEV_GUILD_ID, and DATABASE_URL
Output includes a multi-stage Dockerfile with a non-root user
Output includes a docker-compose.yml with bot and postgres services
Output includes a ban command using SlashCommandBuilder with user and reason options and BanMembers permission
Output includes a warn command that stores warnings in the database
Output includes a purge command with a count option that uses bulkDelete
Output includes a prisma/schema.prisma with GuildConfig and ModAction models using String IDs for Discord snowflakes
Output includes a separate deploy-commands.ts script for registering slash commands
Output includes an interactionCreate event handler with error handling and cooldown logic
Output handles SIGINT and SIGTERM signals for graceful shutdown

evals.prompt: I want to build a Discord bot for my gaming community. It should have an XP/leveling system where people earn XP by chatting, rank cards with a generated image, and role rewards when they hit certain levels. Also need a basic economy with daily rewards and a shop. Use PostgreSQL and Redis. I have about 500 members.
evals.expected_output: A complete bot with leveling and economy systems, including messageCreate XP tracking with cooldowns, rank card image generation, level-up role rewards, economy commands (balance, daily, shop, buy, pay), Prisma schema with UserLevel, LevelReward, UserEconomy, ShopItem models, Redis for cooldowns, and proper anti-exploit measures.

assertions.text: Output includes a messageCreate event handler that awards random XP (15-25 range) with a cooldown
Output includes rank card image generation using @napi-rs/canvas or canvas
Output includes level-up role reward logic that grants roles when users reach configured levels
Output includes balance, daily, shop, and buy slash commands
Output uses Redis for cooldown tracking (daily, work, or XP cooldowns)
Output uses database transactions for balance transfer operations to prevent race conditions
Output includes a leaderboard command with pagination
Prisma schema uses String type for all Discord snowflake IDs, not Int

evals.prompt: Build me a support ticket bot for my SaaS product's Discord server. Users click a button to create a ticket, it makes a private thread, staff can claim tickets, and when closed it generates an HTML transcript. Also need a config command for admins to set up the ticket panel and support role. Deploy with GitHub Actions to my VPS.
evals.expected_output: A ticket system bot with button-based ticket creation, private thread management, claim/close/transcript functionality, admin configuration commands, HTML transcript generation, GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline, and proper permission checks.

assertions.text: Output includes a setup command that sends an embed with a Create Ticket button using ButtonBuilder
Output creates a private thread when the ticket button is clicked
Output includes a ticket claim command or button for staff
Output includes a close command/button that generates a transcript before archiving
Output includes HTML transcript generation (either custom or using discord-html-transcripts)
Output includes admin configuration for support role, log channel, and greeting message
Output includes a .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint, test, and deploy steps
Button interactions use stable customId patterns (not collectors) so they work after bot restarts
Output enforces a per-user limit on open tickets
